definition: Pretense means a false appearance or action intended to deceive — a pretending.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word pretense. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know pretense should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The salesman got inside dozens of homes under the pretense of offering a free safety inspection.
Putting on an act can be as small as hiding a bad mood; a pretense is a false front built specifically to deceive someone.
A masquerade goes further than a pretense — an entire false identity, worn head to toe for as long as the deception needs to last, not just one false front.

A guise is the deceptive outer form something wears — reforms passed under the guise of progress, a spy in the guise of a florist. It points at the costume, the surface itself. A pretense is the pretending: the false front a person keeps up to deceive. The guise is what is worn; the pretense is the performance behind it.

A charade is a false display kept up for show — often an empty performance nobody quite believes, so hollow that onlookers can see through it. A pretense is built to actually deceive: the audience is meant to buy it. Call it a charade to sneer at its emptiness; call it a pretense when the deception is meant to work.

A sham is a fake thing passed off as genuine — a sham marriage, a sham election, a sham trial. The word points at the counterfeit object or institution itself. A pretense is the act of pretending a person keeps up — the false appearance, not the fake article.

The reporter arranged a job interview at the warehouse, but the interview was a pretense — her real goal was to document the unsafe working conditions inside.
The interview looked genuine from the outside, but it was staged to conceal her true purpose.
That false front — an act put on to deceive — is exactly what a pretense is.
Neutral — watch the idiom and the unit-mate
The most common idiom is 'under false pretenses' — gaining something through deception.
And keep pretense apart from its unit-mate pretext (also taught in this unit): a pretext is the fake reason you give for doing something, while a pretense is the fake appearance or act you keep up.

Restaurant critics at the paper worked under strict anonymity, and Dana had turned the required pretense into a small art.
She booked under invented names, dressed to be forgotten, and asked her questions with the vague air of a tourist deciding between desserts.
The performance had one purpose: the kitchen must believe she was nobody, or the meal she reviewed would never be the meal ordinary diners were served.
Once, a maitre d' stared a moment too long, and she complained loudly about parking like every other regular until his attention drifted.
Her editor called it acting; she called it accuracy.
